title: I Reported the Fake Closed Sign on the Only Accessible Restroom

parts.text: I needed the accessible stall at the mall at 1:12 p.m. and found a handwritten CLOSED on the only one with grab bars. The standard stalls were open and filthy. I was thirty-nine, cane user, holding a shopping bag. A barista from the kiosk said they close it so teens do not vape. Teens vape in every stall. I photographed the sign, the open filthy stalls, and the time. Then I asked mall ops, whose number is on the directory, whether closed meant broken. They said they would check. At 1:19 a janitor peeled the sign off, muttered it was just paper, and a manager from the kiosk hissed that I had cost them their quiet office.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The kiosk manager just called the accessible stall their quiet office.

social.video_title: Handwritten CLOSED on the only grab-bar stall — Part 1/2
social.description: Cane, vape excuse, a paper sign. Ops called it a check. Would you have photographed the directory number?

parts.text: Ops logged a facilities ticket. The stall stayed open with an actual out-of-order process if it ever breaks. The kiosk lost the key they were not supposed to have. I used the stall. The filthy standards got a real mop. Quiet office is not a restroom category. Paper signs are not locks. I finished shopping. The directory number still works. I keep it.

social.video_title: They were not supposed to have that key — Part 2/2
social.description: Ticket, mop, no more paper CLOSED. Was vaping a grab bar?
